newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel has no comment on Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel has no comment on Thomson-CSF.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom said it had no comment on a report in the La Tribune newspaper about what it called Alcatel's plan to acquire the state's stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF.

"Until the publication of the conditions of sale (cahier des charges) we make no comment on our plans concerning Thomson-CSF, beyond the interview given by Mr (Serge) Tchuruk to Le Monde recently," an Alcatel spokesman said.
He also declined comment on reports of possible talks between Alcatel and rival bidder Lagardere to see whether a joint bid was possible.
In the Le Monde interview, Tchuruk said he had turned to broader platform for its bid for Thomson-CSF.
La Tribune said plans include a surprise takeover of Thomson-CSF missiles by Aerospatiale in return for part of its own capital.

Under the plan, Alcatel would take between 51-70 percent of Thomson-CSF, while privately-held Dassault Industries, the parent of Dassault Electronique and Dassault Aviation, would gain 10-12 percent, or up to 15 percent.
Aerospatiale, once merged with Dassault, would take seven to 10 percent of the capital, while 25 percent would be quoted on the Paris stock market. Employees would own around five percent.
